strategy.summary: Reproduce by checking out the buggy commit 68640e752e90 of sympy from source with an editable install, then running the developer's new test test_nonlinsolve_issue_28646 in sympy/solvers/tests/test_solveset.py. On the buggy revision nonlinsolve raises a TypeError (RR/EX domain confusion in the Groebner path of _handle_poly) before the assertions run, so the test fails. On the fixed revision the float coefficients are converted with nsimplify before the Groebner basis, the call returns 8 solutions, and the 1e-9 component comparisons pass. No build step is needed for the test; the doc build commands are irrelevant.

pinned_because: No documented dependency constraint for sympy exists in the evidence, so no version pin is applied. The buggy commit itself is installed from source (editable), so the code under test and the test file match the same revision rather than a PyPI release.

mpmath is a runtime dependency of sympy and is pulled in by the editable install; it is listed only so it is visible. No era-inferred pin is used because the PR date (2025-11-29) is not tied to a specific version table entry.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy commit 68640e752e90 the test fails: nonlinsolve(lst, x, y) raises a TypeError from the polynomial domain path, so the test errors before len(res)==8 is checked. On the fixed revision (the commit after the buggy one that applies nsimplify(p.as_expr().evalf(), rational=True) in _handle_poly) the call returns 8 solutions and every res.args[i][j] is within 1e-9 of the reference sol[i][j], so the test passes.
strategy.numerical_probe: Call nonlinsolve on the system from the test, then check len(res) and the absolute difference of each real and complex component against the reference list, with threshold 1e-9.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: TypeError raised from the Groebner/polynomial domain path (RR/EX confusion), reported as exception

risks: The test indexes res.args[i][j] positionally against a fixed reference list, so the fixed code must return solutions in the same order; a correct but reordered result would fail the test on the fixed revision.

The evidence gives no python version, platform, or architecture; the defect is only described for this specific system, so it is not known whether it reproduces on other platforms or BLAS/mpmath builds. If the failure depends on a platform-specific floating-point result, it may not transition as expected.

The NaN remark in the PR discussion is not tied to a specific expression in the evidence, so the exact NaN-producing step cannot be checked; the plan relies only on the TypeError and the test transition.

The 1e-9 absolute tolerance on float-derived solutions is tight; numerical noise from different mpmath versions could cause the fixed revision to fail the comparison even when the solutions are correct.

The buggy commit is assumed to be the direct parent of the fix; if the buggy commit is not that parent, the checkout must be adjusted so the test file and the code under test are at the correct before/after revisions.
No sanitiser or special compiler is needed, since sympy is pure Python; if a build with a compiled extension is required in a different environment, that is not stated in the evidence.

oracle.tolerance: abs(res.args[i][j] - sol[i][j]) < 1e-9 for each component of each of the 8 solutions
oracle.reference_source: Reference list 'sol' in test_nonlinsolve_issue_28646 in the developer's PR diff
oracle.why: Solutions are floating-point (and complex) values, so exact equality is not meaningful; the test checks absolute error per component against the 1e-9 bound.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy commit nonlinsolve raises a TypeError inside the Groebner basis path (RR/EX domain confusion in _handle_poly), so the call does not return and pytest reports the test as failed/errored before len(res)==8 or the component comparisons are reached.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed commit the float coefficients are converted via nsimplify before the Groebner basis, nonlinsolve returns 8 solutions in the reference order, len(res)==8 holds, and all components are within 1e-9 of the reference, so the test passes.
